mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a supply shock with rising commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations fall sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% combined with a concurrent decline in industrial production of more than 0.5% for three months signals a synchronized labor and supply downturn, which reduces earnings and increases recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% AND INDPRO falls >0.5% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong technological innovation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which dampens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a fiscal stimulus period.
